definition: A person who derives sexual pleasure from receiving pain, humiliation, or subjugation.
notes: Used both in clinical psychology and casual Brazilian conversation; the scientific-sounding suffix gives it a moderately technical register despite widespread lay use.

definition: Sexual gratification derived from inflicting pain, humiliation, or suffering on another person.
notes: More clinical-sounding than most kink vocabulary; used by psychologists, kink communities, and educated laypeople alike. Named after the Marquis de Sade.

definition: A person who derives pleasure from inflicting pain or humiliation; also used adjectivally for any cruel or punishing behavior, sexual or otherwise.
notes: Gender-inflected: sádico (masculine), sádica (feminine). Frequently used outside sexual contexts to describe general cruelty, which dilutes the kink-specific signal.

definition: The sexual practice of inserting an entire hand or fist into a partner's vagina or anus, used as a direct English loanword.
notes: No common native Portuguese equivalent in circulation; the English loanword dominates. Recognition skews toward sexually experienced adults and LGBTQ+ communities; lower among conservative or older demographics.

definition: Erotic spanking of a partner for sexual arousal, used as a direct English loanword in Brazilian BDSM communities.
notes: Native equivalents include 'surra' and 'palmada'; the English loanword is preferred in kink-community and pornographic contexts. Recognition higher among younger and internet-connected Brazilians.

definition: In BDSM contexts, an erotic beating or impact-play session; in general Brazilian Portuguese, any severe physical thrashing or defeat.
notes: Primary meaning is non-sexual (sports, fights, punishment); the BDSM meaning is a register shift via context. The word is never inherently sexual — only context disambiguates. Highly recognizable universally.

definition: A whip used in BDSM impact play to strike a partner's body for erotic stimulation or discipline; also the standard Brazilian Portuguese word for any whip.
notes: Technically denotes a single-tail whip, not a multi-tailed flogger; mapped to bdsm_flogger as the nearest registry concept covering whip-type BDSM implements. In everyday language refers to any whipping instrument (horsewhip, riding crop, etc.).

definition: Handcuffs used in erotic restraint or bondage play; also the standard Brazilian Portuguese word for police or restraint handcuffs.
notes: Universally recognized as the word for handcuffs; the BDSM meaning is a direct transfer of the primary denotation into an erotic context. No inherent sexual meaning — fully context-dependent.

definition: A gag device used in BDSM to silence or restrain a partner's ability to speak; also the standard Brazilian Portuguese word for any gag or muzzle.
notes: No gag-specific concept in the canonical registry; mapped to bondage as the nearest category. Covers all gag types (ball gag, bit gag, tape). The word is also used in political speech to mean censorship or silencing.

definition: Rope used in sexual bondage to physically restrain a partner for erotic purposes; also the standard everyday Brazilian Portuguese word for any rope or cord.
notes: One of the most common words in Portuguese repurposed for BDSM; in kink contexts often implies shibari-style aesthetics. The English compound 'bondage rope' captures the full concept; 'corda' alone only signals the tool.

definition: Sexual activity in which participants adopt fictional personas, characters, or scenarios to enact erotic fantasies; used as a direct English loanword in Brazilian Portuguese.
notes: No sexual_roleplay slug in canonical registry; mapped to bdsm_play as nearest structured consensual play concept. Role play is broader than BDSM but overlaps heavily in Brazilian kink communities. The native equivalent 'jogo de papéis' is less common.

definition: In sexual contexts, an erotic fantasy or imaginative scenario used for arousal; in general use, the everyday Portuguese word for fantasy or imagination.
notes: Not inherently sexual; meaning is fully determined by context. Mapped to eroticism as nearest registry concept — no sexual_fantasy slug exists in the registry. Low crude score because the word itself is completely neutral; it is the context that sexualizes it.

definition: A sexual fantasy; an erotic imaginative scenario deliberately constructed for arousal, often shared with a partner or enacted in role play.
notes: The 'sexual' modifier removes all ambiguity. More deliberate and plannable in connotation than 'fantasia' alone — implies a scenario that could potentially be enacted. Mapped to eroticism as nearest registry concept.

definition: Literally 'game of roles'; the native Brazilian Portuguese phrase for sexual role play, in which participants adopt fictional personas or scenarios for erotic purposes.
notes: Less common than the English loanword 'role play' in Brazilian kink communities; sounds slightly more formal or pedagogical. Mapped to bdsm_play as nearest registry concept. Recognition lower because Brazilians typically use the English loanword in kink contexts.

definition: Group sex; sexual activity involving three or more participants simultaneously or in overlapping encounters.
notes: Neutral descriptive compound; less charged than 'orgia' or 'gangbang'. Functions as the default everyday Brazilian Portuguese descriptor for multi-partner sex when a neutral register is intended.

definition: A sexual act in which one person is simultaneously or sequentially engaged sexually by multiple partners; used as a direct English loanword.
notes: Among the cruder English loanwords in Brazilian sexual vocabulary; used in pornographic taxonomy and crude casual speech. No widely-used native Portuguese equivalent exists. Recognition highest among young adults and regular pornography consumers.

definition: An orgy; a sexual gathering involving multiple participants freely engaging with each other in an unstructured or celebratory atmosphere.
notes: Derives from Latin/Greek 'orgia' (secret Bacchic rites); carries historical connotations of excess, debauchery, and transgression beyond mere group sex. More evocative and colorful than 'sexo em grupo'.

definition: Literally 'couple exchange'; the standard Brazilian Portuguese euphemism for swinging, in which couples consensually swap sexual partners.
notes: Preferred in-community term among Brazilian swingers; sounds considerably less sexually explicit than 'swing' or 'orgia' in casual conversation, functioning as an effective euphemism. 'Clubes de troca de casais' are a well-documented institution in Brazil.

definition: The swinging lifestyle; consensual sexual partner-swapping between couples, used as an English loanword in Brazilian Portuguese.
notes: Used as noun ('entrar no swing', 'mundo do swing') and attributively ('clube de swing'). Coexists with 'troca de casais'; 'swing' is the loanword form while 'troca de casais' is the native phrasing. Brazil has a particularly active swinger community.

definition: A person who participates in the swinging lifestyle, engaging in consensual sexual partner-swapping with other couples.
notes: Used unchanged from English; forms the identity noun for practitioners of 'swing'. Recognized primarily among those familiar with the lifestyle, adult entertainment media, or tabloid journalism.

definition: A man who derives erotic pleasure from his partner having sex with other men; used as an English loanword in Brazilian kink and pornographic communities.
notes: The English loanword coexists with the native term 'corno'; 'cuckold' is used specifically in kink-community and pornographic contexts with the fetish-positive connotation, while 'corno' carries the primary meaning of a shamed, deceived husband.

definition: In fetish contexts, a man whose partner has sex with other men with his knowledge and erotic pleasure; in general Brazilian Portuguese, a highly offensive slur for a man being cheated on.
notes: Literally 'horn' (referencing the cuckold's horns of European tradition). The same word functions as both a severe insult (cheated-on husband who doesn't know or is helpless) and a kink identity term — the fetish register is a deliberate reappropriation. Near-universal recognition. Crude score reflects the insult register, which is primary.

definition: A married woman who has sex with men other than her husband with his full knowledge and enthusiastic consent, framed as shared erotic pleasure for both spouses.
notes: More niche than 'cuckold' or 'swing'; primarily recognized in Brazilian swinger, cuckold, and online pornography communities. Conceptually distinct from 'troca de casais' in that only the wife has additional partners while the husband watches or otherwise participates vicariously.

definition: A sexual encounter involving exactly three participants; a French loanword used in Brazilian Portuguese as a sophisticated or euphemistic alternative to 'sexo a três'.
notes: French for 'household of three'; used across many languages as an elegant or ironic euphemism for a threesome. In Brazilian Portuguese carries a slightly refined or humorous register relative to the blunter native alternative. Often written without the grave accent on 'à' in Brazilian usage.

definition: Literally 'sex at/with three'; the standard colloquial Brazilian Portuguese phrase for a sexual encounter involving exactly three participants.
notes: The everyday Brazilian Portuguese descriptor for a threesome; more direct and less euphemistic than 'ménage a três'. The preposition 'a' (at/with) is the standard construction; 'sexo a três' functions as the default neutral phrasing across all demographics familiar with the concept.
